 IMPACT Magazine 
 CapCon Wins Award for Exposing SNAP Fraud
 November 3, 2026 
 | 
 Font size: 
 75% 
 100% 
 125% 
 150% 
 By Scott McClallen 
 Michigan Capitol Confidential won the 2026
Marketing Campaign of the Year award from the
State Policy Network this August for our 30-story
series exposing fraud in the Supplemental Nutrition
Assistance Program.
 SNAP helps poor Michiganders buy groceries at
10,000 retailers statewide, but thieves across the
United States and even overseas steal benefits through
card skimmers installed in gas stations, grocery stores,
liquor stores and other public places. Those devices
copy SNAP card data that the criminals sell online,
leaving Michigan families hungry.
 We found a 400% increase in skimmer fraud from 2023-24. Criminals stole benefits so frequently that Michigan mailed an average of 738 replacement Bridge cards every day in 2024. 
 CapCon was the only outlet in Michigan digging into
SNAP fraud, and our stories influenced Michigan
lawmakers to spend $17 million to upgrade SNAP
cards for 1.3 million people.
 We filed hundreds of public records requests, seeking
information from federal, state, and local officials
as we tried to discover the severity of the problem.
We staked out discount retailers like Sam’s Club and
Costco for hours, looking for people pushing carts
piled high with energy drinks, diapers, and baby
formula — highly resalable items. We read over 500
pages of police reports detailing SNAP fraud in
Oakland County, and fought Wayne County,
which claims that it doesn’t have a single
document about SNAP fraud, even
though it is the state’s most
populated county.
 The State Policy Network award recognizes
campaigns that achieve real-world results, and our
work paid off.
 In 2025, the state reported $7.7 million in SNAP
fraud, down from $14 million in 2024. Michigan
has mailed upgraded cards to most people in the
program, which should reduce fraud even more.
 In some cases, we found that Michigan paid SNAP
benefits to people who weren’t eligible. Michigan
has paid more than $4 million in SNAP benefits
since 2024 to people with out-of-state addresses.
 Michigan is now the first state in the Midwest to
upgrade its SNAP cards. Ohio and New York are
copying Michigan’s playbook to upgrade cards,
further showing CapCon’s worth.
